50:1: The people of interpretation differed regarding his saying Qaf. Some of them said: It is one of the names of God Almighty, by which He swore. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Qaf, Nun, and similar words, for it is an oath that God has sworn, and it is one of the names of God. Others said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Qaf, he said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an. Others said: Qaf is the name of the mountain surrounding the earth. Our explanation of the interpretation of the letters of the alphabet at the beginning of the chapters of the Qur’an has been presented before, sufficiently so that we do not need to repeat it here. And his saying, And the Glorious Qur’an, means: And the Noble Qur’an. Abu Kurayb told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Ishaq, on the authority of Ja’ar bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr: “Qaf. By the Glorious Qur’an.” He said: The Noble Qur’an. The Arabists differed about the position of the answer to this oath. Some of the grammarians of Basra said, Qaf, by the Glorious Qur’an, is an oath based on His statement, We know what the earth takes away from them. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said, It contains the meaning by which He swore. He said, He mentioned that it was decreed by God. He said, “It is said that Qaf is a mountain surrounding the earth. If that is the case, then it is as if it is in the nominative case: that is, it is Qaf, by God.” He said, “Its nominative case should have been made clear because it is a noun and not a spelling. He said, “Perhaps Qaf alone was mentioned in its noun, as the poet said: I told her to stand for us, she said stand The letter Qaf was mentioned to indicate that Qaf is from the word “stop”, meaning that I am standing. This statement is, in our view, the more correct of the two statements, because the word qad is not known in the answers to oaths. Rather, oaths are answered if they are answered with one of the four letters: lam, “in,” ma, and la, or if their answer is omitted, then it is invalid.
50:2: And His statement, Rather, they were amazed that a warner had come to them from among themselves, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, "O Muhammad, the polytheists of your people did not lie to you, because they did not know that you were truthful and just, but they lied to you out of amazement that a warner had come to them warning them of God's punishment from among them, meaning a human being from among the children of Adam, and that no angel had come to them with a message from God." And His statement, Then the disbelievers said, ‘This is an amazing thing.’ God Almighty says: The disbelievers from among the Quraysh said when a warner came to them from among themselves, This is an amazing thing. That is, the coming of a man from among us from among Adam with God’s message to us, Why was an angel not sent down to him to be with him as a warner?
50:3: The speaker says: The resurrection was not mentioned, so he tells about these people’s disbelief in what they called for, so what is the point of reporting about them that they denied what they did not call for, and their response to what they were not asked about? It was said: The Arab scholars differed on this, so we will mention what they said on this, then we will follow it with the explanation, God willing. One of the grammarians of Basra said about this: If we die and become dust, is that a far-fetched return? He did not mention that he returned, and that, and God knows best, was in response, as if it was said to them: You will return, so they said: If we die and become dust, is that a far-fetched return? And one of the grammarians of Kufa said: His statement: If we die and become dust is a statement before which it was not clear what this could be an answer to, but its meaning is implied, and God knows best: “Qaf. By the Glorious Qur’an” You will be resurrected after death, so they said: If we are dust, will we be resurrected? They denied the resurrection, then said, That is a far-fetched return. They denied it entirely, and his saying, far-fetched, is like saying to a man who makes a mistake in a matter: You have gone a long way from the truth, meaning you have made a mistake. And the correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that in this speech there is something omitted and the evidence of what was mentioned is sufficient to support its mention. That is because God indicated with His report of the denial of these polytheists, with whom He began this surah with the report of their denial of His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with His saying, “Rather, they are amazed that a warner has come to them from among themselves. So the disbelievers say, ‘This is an amazing thing,’” His threat to them for their denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is as if He said to them, if they say, denying the message of God, His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, This is an amazing thing, you will know, O people, when you are resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, what your state will be in your denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and your denial of his prophethood. So they said, responding to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, When we die and become dust, we know that, and we see what you promised us for your denial. That is a far-fetched return, meaning that that will not happen, and we will not return alive after our death. So He was sufficient with the evidence of His saying, Rather, they are amazed that A warner came to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers said, “This is an amazing thing. And in what was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, he said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, When we die and become dust, is that a far-fetched return? They said: How can God protect you when we have become bones and dust, and have wandered in the earth? This is evidence of the truth of what we said, that they denied the resurrection when they were threatened with it.
50:4: And His statement, We know what the earth takes from them, God Almighty says: We know what the earth consumes of their bodies after their death, what the earth consumes and destroys of their bodies, and they have a written record, along with Our knowledge of that, preserving all of that. God Almighty called it the Preserver, because what is written in it does not fade away, nor does it change or alter. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, We know what the earth takes away from them, means: What the earth consumes of their flesh, skin, bones, and hair. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, What the earth diminishes of them, he said: Of their bones. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, We know what the earth takes away from them, meaning: what the earth consumes from them. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: We know what the earth takes away from them. He said: It means death. He said: Who among them dies, or he said: What the earth consumes from them when they die. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: God said, We know what the earth takes of them, meaning: what the earth consumes of them, and we know about it, and they are with me, along with my knowledge of them, in a preserved book.
50:5: God Almighty says: What happened to these polytheists who said, When we die and become dust, is that a far-fetched return? in their saying this? Rather, they denied the truth, which is the Qur’an, when it came to them from God. Like what Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, meaning they denied the truth when it came to them, meaning they denied the Qur’an. So they are in a confused matter, he says: They are in a confused and ambiguous matter, they do not know what is right from what is wrong. It is said that the matter of the people has become confused if it is mixed up and neglected. The interpretation of the verse has been interpreted differently by the commentators, although they have similar meanings. Some of them said: Its meaning is: They are in a reprehensible matter. He said: Al-Marij is the reprehensible thing. Who said that? Muhammad bin Khalid bin Khidash told me: Salma bin Qutaybah told me, on the authority of Wahb bin Habib Al-Amidi, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he was asked about his statement, A disturbing matter. He said: Disturbing is the reprehensible thing. Haven’t you heard the poet say: Suddenly, she sought him with her innermost being, and he became proud like a thread of silk. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: in a different matter. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, in a matter of doubt, meaning: different. Others said: Rather, it means: in a matter of misguidance. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are in a confused matter. He said: He said: They are in a matter of misguidance. Others said: Rather, it means: in an ambiguous matter. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Ishaq, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, regarding his statement, So they are in a confused matter, he said: Confused. Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, A confused matter, he said: Ambiguous. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, They are in a confused matter, meaning that the matter is unclear to them. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, who said: His religion became confusing to him. Others said: Rather, it is mixed. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, in a confused matter, he said: Confused means mixed. I said: Although these expressions differ in wording, they are similar in meaning, because something is different and ambiguous, and its meaning is problematic. If it is like that, it is reprehensible, because what is known is clear and obvious. If it is unknown, then it is undoubtedly misguidance, because guidance is clear and unambiguous.
50:6: And His statement, Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We constructed it? God Almighty says: Have these deniers of resurrection after death, who deny Our ability to revive them after their affliction, not looked at the sky above them, how We constructed it? So We proportioned it as a protected ceiling, and adorned it with stars. “And it has no rifts.” Meaning: It has no cracks or fissures. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, of the clefts, he said: split. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And it has no rifts. I said to him, meaning Ibn Zayd: Are rifts something that is disassociated from one another? He said: Yes.
50:7: And His statement, And the earth We have spread out, meaning: And the earth We have spread out. And We cast therein firm mountains, meaning: And We placed therein firm mountains, firmly planted in the earth. And We caused to grow therein of every beautiful kind, meaning: And We caused to grow in the earth of every kind of beautiful plant, which is the beautiful. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Bahij meaning: beautiful. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We cast therein firm mountains, and firm mountains are mountains, and We caused to grow therein of every beautiful kind, meaning of every beautiful kind. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: I said to Ibn Zayd al-Bahij: Is it good looking? He said: Yes.
50:8: And His statement, As insight, means: We did that as insight for you, O people, so that He may make you aware of your Lord’s power over whatever He wills. And a reminder for every servant who turns back, means: And a reminder from God of His greatness and power, and an alert to His Oneness. For every servant who turns back, means: For every servant who returns to faith in God and acts in obedience to Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, insight: a blessing from God that the servants see. And a reminder for every servant who turns in repentance: meaning one who turns with his heart to God. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Insight and Reminder, he said: Insight from God. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, insight, he said: insight. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ata’ and Mujahid: For every servant who turns back. They said: One who responds.
50:9: God Almighty says, And We sent down water from the sky, blessed rain, and with it We caused orchards of trees to grow, and the harvested grain of wheat, barley, and all kinds of grains. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And the grain of the harvest means wheat and barley. Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And the grain of the harvest He said: It is wheat and barley. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid: And the grain of the harvest he said: wheat. Some Arab scholars used to say in his statement, And the grain of the harvest, that the grain is the harvest, and it is one of the things that is attributed to itself, like his statement, Indeed, this is the absolute truth (al-Waqi’ah 56:95).
50:10: And his saying, And tall palm trees, means: And We caused to grow, with the water which We sent down from the sky, tall palm trees. Tall means tall. A tall mountain is called a tall mountain, as Abu Nawfal said to Abu Hubayrah: O son of those who, by their grace, brought the river to Qais Fazara And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, tall, meaning tall. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the tall palm trees, he said: Tall palm trees. Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, regarding his statement, And the tall palm trees, he said: In their trunks means their height in standing. Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And tall palm trees. Tall means tall. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, tall and tall. He said: tall. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And the tall palm trees. He said: With their stems, their height. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the tall palm trees. He said: It means their height. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, and tall palm trees, that tall means tall. His saying, Its dates are arranged in layers, means: This tall palm tree has dates, which are the Kafranbel. Arranged: he says: arranged one on top of the other, overlapping. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It has a date palm in layers. He said: He says one part on top of the other. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Nadid, he said: Arranged. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: It has a cluster of dates. He said: Some of it is on top of others. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: It has a date palm in layers meaning it is arranged one on top of the other.
50:11: And His statement, provision for the servants, means: We created with this water that We sent down from the sky these gardens, the grain and the palm trees as sustenance for the servants, some of it as food, and some of it as fruit and enjoyment. And His statement, And We revived thereby a dead land, God Almighty says, And We revived thereby a dead land that had become barren and dry, with no plants or vegetation. And His statement, Likewise is the emergence, God Almighty says: Just as We caused this dead land to grow with this water, and revived it with it, and brought forth its plants and its crops, thus We will bring you forth on the Day of Resurrection alive from your graves after your affliction in them with what descends upon it of water.
50:12: God Almighty says, You have denied before these polytheists who denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his people, the people of Noah and the companions of the Messenger. We have already mentioned before the matter of the companions of the Messenger, and that they were a people who threw their prophet into a well. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Abu Bakr on the authority of Ikrimah on the same authority. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The Companions of Al-Rass, and Al-Rass is a well in which the companion of Yasin was killed. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The Companions of the Well, he said: A well. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Amr ibn al-Harith told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Amr ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Qatada, who said: The people of the thicket - the thicket means the destroyed trees - and the people of the tree were two nations. Then God sent to them one prophet, Shu`ayb, and God punished them with two punishments: And Thamud, and `Ad, and Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lot, and the people of the thicket, who were the people of Shu`ayb, and their story has already passed, and the people of Tubba’. The people of Tubba were idolaters. As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq. His story and the story of his people were as follows: Mujahid bin Musa told us: Yazid told us: Imran bin Hudayr told us on the authority of Abu Majlaz on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he asked Abdullah bin Salam, what was Tubba’? He said: Tubba’ was a man from the Arabs, and he gained power over the people, so he chose young men from the best, and kept them company and brought them in, until he took from them and pledged allegiance to them. His people were arrogant about that and said: He has abandoned your religion and pledged allegiance to the young men. When that became widespread, he said to the young men, and the young men said: Between us and them is the fire, which burns the liar and saves the truthful from it. So they did, and the young men hung their copies of the Qur’an around their necks, then they went to the fire, and when they were about to enter it, the fire scorched their faces, so they turned back from it. Tubba’ said to them: You must enter it. So when they entered it, it opened up to them until they cut it open. And he said to his al-Nas 114:Enter it. So when they were about to enter it, the fire scorched their faces, so they turned back from it. Tubba’ said to him: You must enter it. So when they entered it, it opened up to them, until when they reached the middle, it surrounded them and burned them. So Tubba’ became a Muslim, and Tubba’ was a righteous man. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Malik bin Tha’labah bin Abi Malik Al-Qurazi, who said: I heard Ibrahim bin Muhammad Al-Qurazi, who said: I heard Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Talha bin Abdullah narrating that when Tubba’ approached Yemen to enter it, Himyar prevented him from doing so and said: Do not enter it upon us, for you have abandoned our religion. So he called them to his religion and said: It is a religion better than your religion. They said: Then judge us by the Fire! He said: Yes. He said: And in Yemen, as the people of Yemen claim, there was a fire that judged between them in what they differed about, devouring the oppressor and not harming the oppressed. When they said that to Tubba’, he said: You have been fair. So his people went out with their idols and what they used to draw near to God in their religion. He said: And the two rabbis went out with their copies of the Qur’an around their necks, wearing them with chains of mail, until they sat for the fire at the exit from which it emerged. Then the fire came out to them, and when it approached them, they turned away from it and feared it. So they threw stones at those who were present among the people and ordered them to be patient with it. So they were patient until it covered them and devoured the idols and what they had drawn near to God with it, and some of the men of Himyar. Then the two rabbis went out with their copies of the Qur’an around their necks, and the sweat on their foreheads did not harm them. Then Himyar adhered to its religion. From there and other than that, the origin of Judaism was in Yemen. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the authority of some of his companions that the two rabbis and those who went out with them from Himyar only followed the fire to destroy it, and they said: Whoever destroys it is more deserving of the right. So some men from Himyar approached them with their idols to destroy it, but it approached them to consume them, but they turned away and were unable to destroy it. The two rabbis approached it after that and began to recite the Torah, and it retreated until they restored it to the place from which it had emerged. At that time, it adhered to their religion. Ri’am was a house of theirs that they venerated, and they slaughtered animals at it and spoke from it, since they were still polytheists. The two rabbis said to Tubba’: He is only a devil who helps them and plays with them, so leave us alone with him. He said: Do what you can with him. So they extracted from it, as the people of Yemen claim, a black dog, and slaughtered it. Then they demolished that house, and its remains are today in Yemen, as I was told. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Lahi’ah said on the authority of Amr ibn Jabir al-Hadrami, who told him: I heard Sahl ibn Sa’d al-Sa’idi narrating on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Do not curse Tubba’, for he had become a Muslim. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told me on the authority of Al-Harith Ibn Yazid that Shu’ayb Ibn Zur’ah Al-Ma’afari told him: I heard Abdullah Ibn Amr Ibn Al-As, and a man said to him: Himyar claims that Tubba’ is from them. He said: Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, and he is among the Arabs like the nose between the eyes, and there were seventy kings from them. And His statement, Everyone who denied the messengers, then the threat is justified, means that the Most High says: Every one of those whom We mentioned denied the messengers whom He sent. So the threat is justified, meaning: The threat We promised them for their disbelief in God became necessary for them, and the punishment and vengeance were brought upon them. Our Lord, may He be glorified, placed what He placed in this verse of His punishment upon those who denied the messengers, as a warning to the polytheists of Quraysh and to inform them that if they do not repent from their denial of His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, then He will bring upon them a punishment similar to the one that He brought upon them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So the threat came true, he said: What they were destroyed with was a warning to these people.
50:13: God Almighty said: And Aad, Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lot.
50:14: And the Almighty said: And the companions of the thicket and the people of Tubba’ - all denied the messengers, so my threat came true.
50:15: This is a rebuke from God to the polytheists of Quraysh who said: If we die and become dust, is that a far-fetched return? God, the Most High, says to them: We were exhausted by inventing the first creation which We created when it was nothing, so we are exhausted by bringing them back as a new creation after they have decayed in the dust and perished. He says: That does not exhaust Us, rather We are able to do it. And we bark what we said in that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Are We tired with the first creation? He said: The first creation did not tire us. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Are We weary with the first creation? He said: Are We weary when We created you as a new creation, so you doubt the resurrection? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Maysarah: Are We weary with the first creation? He said: We created you. And His statement, Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation, God Almighty says: These polytheists who deny the resurrection do not doubt that We did not fail in the first creation, but they are in doubt about Our ability to create them a new creation after their annihilation and their trial in their graves. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation, meaning: in doubt about the resurrection. Ibn Haimed told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Maysar: Rather, they are in confusion. He said: The disbelievers. From a new creation. He said: That they will be created after death. Bishr told us: Szsd told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Rather, they are in confusion: meaning, doubt - and the new creation: the resurrection after death - so people became two types of al-Nas 114:those who deny and those who believe. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, In confusion of a new creation, he said: Resurrection after death.
50:16: And His statement, And We have certainly created man and We know what his soul whispers to him, God Almighty says: And We have certainly created man and We know what his soul whispers to him, so nothing is hidden from Us about his secrets and the secrets of his heart. And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein, meaning: We are nearer to man than his neck's rope. The jugular vein is a vein between the throat and the larynx, and the jugular vein is the vein, so it was attributed to itself because of the difference in the pronunciation of its two names. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein, meaning: the vein of the neck. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The jugular vein he said: The one that is in the throat. The Arab scholars differed over the meaning of his statement, And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein. Some of them said: It means: We have more control over him and are closer to him in terms of our ability to control him. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein with knowledge of what his soul whispers to him.
50:17: God Almighty says: And We are nearer to man than his jugular vein, when the two angels receive him, and they are the receivers sitting on the right and on the left. It was said that what is meant by sitting is the watcher. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Sitting, he said: Watching. The Arabists differed about the reason for the singularization of qa’id, and two recipients were mentioned before. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It was said: On the right and on the left qa’id, and he did not say: On the right qa’id, and on the left qa’id, meaning one of them. Then he dispensed with it, as he said: We will bring you forth as children then he dispensed with the singular for the plural, as he said: If they willingly give up to you anything of it and some of the grammarians of Kufa said: qa’id means: sitting on the right and on the left, so he made fa’il a plural, as the messenger makes the people for the two. God Almighty said: Indeed, we are the messenger of the Lord of the worlds to Moses and his brother, and the poet said: But I am the best messenger to know the details of the report So the Messenger made it for the group, so this is a face, and if you wish you can make the one who is sitting one, as it is sufficient for him from his companion, as the poet said: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs And from it is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: I guarantee to whoever comes to me what he has earned and he refuses, and I am not treacherous. He did not say: two traitors.
50:18: And His statement, Not a word does he utter except that there is a watcher by him ready to record it. God Almighty says: Not a word does a person utter, except that when he utters it, there is a watcher ready to record it. That is, a preservation that preserves it, ready and prepared. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: On the right and on the left, Qa’id. He said: On the right, which writes down the good deeds, and on the left, which writes down the bad deeds. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taimi, regarding His statement, When the two receivers meet, sitting on the right and on the left, he said: The one on the right is a commander or a trustee over the one on the left. So if the servant does something bad, the one on the right says to the one on the left: Stop! Perhaps he will repent. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: When the two receivers will receive, seated on the right and on the left. He said: An angel will be on his right and another on his left. As for the one on his right, he will write down the good, and as for the one on his left, he will write down the evil. He said: Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Mansour on the authority of Mujahid who said: With every person are two angels: one on his right and one on his left. He said: As for the one on his right, he writes down the good, and as for the one on his left, he writes down the evil. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We have certainly created man and We know what his soul whispers to him… to at-Tid. He said: God has appointed two guardians over the son of Adam at night and two guardians during the day, who record his deeds and write down his traces. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: When the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left, until he reached prepared. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: He does not utter a word, meaning he does not speak anything but it is written down for him. Ikrimah used to say: That is only in the case of good and evil, they are written down for him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Al-Hasan recited: On the right and on the left is seated. He said: Then he said: O son of Adam, a scroll has been spread out for you, and two noble angels have been assigned to you, one on your right and the other on your left. The one on your right will record your good deeds, and the one on your left will record your bad deeds. So do whatever you wish, whether it is little or much, until when you die, your scroll will be folded and placed around your neck with you in your grave, until you emerge on the Day of Resurrection. At that time, He will say: And every man We have fastened his fate to his neck... until He reached an accountant. God has made you the accountant of yourself. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, On the right and on the left, sitting. He said: The scribe of good deeds is on his right, and the scribe of bad deeds is on his left. He said: Mihran narrated to us on the authority of Sufyan, who said: I was informed that the scribe of good deeds is a leader over the scribe of bad deeds. So if someone sins, he says to him: Do not be hasty! Perhaps he will seek forgiveness. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Not a word does he utter but there is a watcher by him ready to record it, he said: He placed with him someone who writes down everything he utters, and he is a watcher with him. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Amr ibn al-Harith told me on the authority of Hisham al-Himsi, that he had heard that if a man commits a sin, the scribe on the right says to the one on the left: Write. He says: No, you write. They both refuse, so a caller calls out: O scribe on the left, write what the scribe on the right omitted.
50:19: And in His statement, And the intoxication of death will come with the truth, there are two aspects of interpretation. The first is that the intoxication of death, which is its severity and its overwhelming power over man's understanding, like intoxication from sleep or drink, will come with the truth of the matter of the Hereafter, thus alerting man so that he may be certain of it and know it. The second is that the intoxication of death will come with the reality of death. It was mentioned about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, that he was reading and the intoxication of truth came with death. The narration mentioned that: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Wasil, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, who said: When Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was giving judgment, Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: This is like what the poet said: If one day he is gathered and his chest is constricted Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: Do not say that. Rather, it is as God the Almighty said: “And the intoxication of truth has come with death. That is what you were avoiding.” It has been mentioned that this is also the way Ibn Mas`ud read it. There are two interpretations for the way in which someone reads it: One of them is: And the intoxication of God came with death, so the truth is God Almighty. The second is: That the intoxication is death, attributed to itself, as it was said: Indeed, this is the certain truth, so the interpretation of the statement is: And the true intoxication came with death. His saying, That is what you were avoiding, means: This intoxication that has come to you, O human being, is the truth that you were running away from and evading.
50:20: And His saying, And the Trumpet will be blown, that will be the Day of Threat. We have already explained the meaning of the Trumpet and how it will be blown, by mentioning the differences of opinion among those who differ, which is the most correct of the opinions in our view, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And His saying, That is the Day of Threat, means: This day on which the trumpet will be blown is the Day of Threat on which God promised the infidels that He would punish them.
50:21: God Almighty says: And there will come a Day when the Trumpet will be blown. Every soul will have its Lord, with it a driver who will drive it to God, and a witness who will testify about it as to what it did in this world, whether good or evil. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Yahya bin Rafi’, a freed slave of Thaqeef, who said: I heard Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, giving a sermon, and he recited this verse: A driver and a witness. He said: A driver who drives her to God, and a witness who testifies against her regarding what she did. He said: Hakam told us on the authority of Ismail on the authority of Abu Isa who said: I heard Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, giving a sermon, and he recited this verse: And every soul will come with a driver and a witness. He said: The driver drives it to the command of God, and the witness testifies against it regarding what it did. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And every soul will come with a driver and a witness. He said: The driver is from the angels, and the witness is a witness against him from within himself. Ibn Hamid told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mihran, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: A driver and a witness means a driver who drives her to the command of God, and a witness who testifies against her regarding what she did. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: A driver and a witness: a driver who drives her to the command of God, and a witness who testifies against her regarding what she did. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid regarding the statement of God, a driver and a witness, he said: The two angels are: a writer and a witness. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And every soul will come with a driver and a witness, he said: A driver will drive it to its Lord, and a witness will testify to its deeds. Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman ibn Harb told us: Abu Hilal told us: Qatada told us regarding His statement, And every soul will come with a driver and a witness, he said: A driver will drive it to its account, and a witness will testify against it regarding what it did. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan: With her is a driver and a witness. He said: A driver who drives her and a witness who testifies to her actions. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas: A driver and a witness. He said: A driver who drives it, and a witness who testifies to its actions. Al-Husayn narrated: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And every soul will come with a driver and a witness, that the driver is from the angels, and the witness from among themselves is their hands and feet. The angels are also witnesses over them. Yunus told me: Al-Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, A driver and a witness, that he said: An angel is assigned to him who counts his deeds, and an angel drives him to the place of assembly until he meets the place of assembly on the Day of Resurrection. The interpreters of the Quran differed regarding the meaning of these verses. Some of them said: It refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of them said: It refers to the polytheists. Some of them said: It refers to everyone. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Yaqub ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri told me: I asked Zayd ibn Aslam about the statement of God, And the stupor of death will come in truth… the verse, until the statement, a driver and a witness. I said to him: Who is meant by this? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said to him: The Messenger of God? He said: What do you deny? God, the Almighty, said: Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter? And found you lost and guided you. (Al-Baqara: 10) He said: Then I asked Salih ibn Kaysan about it, and he said to me: Have you asked anyone? I said: Yes, I asked Zayd ibn Aslam about it, and he said: What did he say to you? I said: Rather, tell me what you say. He said: I will tell you my opinion, which is my opinion, so tell me what he said to you. I said: He said: This means the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: What does Zayd know? By God, he is not of high age, nor is he eloquent in tongue, nor does he know the Arabic language. Rather, this means an unbeliever. Then he said: Read what comes after it, and it will guide you to that. He said: Then I asked Husayn ibn Abdullah ibn Ubaydullah ibn Abbas, and he said to me the same as Salih had said. Did you ask anyone and they told me about it? I said: I asked Zayd ibn Aslam and Salih ibn Kaysan, and he said to me: What did they say to you? I said: Rather, you should tell me what you said. He said: I will tell you what I said. So I told him what they both said to me. He said: I will disagree with them both, meaning the righteous and the wicked. God said: “And the intoxication of death will come in truth. That is what you were avoiding.” So We have removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp. He said: So the covering was removed from the righteous and the wicked, and they saw everything that would lead to it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And every soul will come with a driver and a witness, meaning the polytheists. The first and most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the one that says: It refers to the righteous and the wicked, because God followed these verses with His statement: And We have certainly created man and We know what his soul whispers to him. Man in this passage means: all people, not specifying some of them over others. So if that is the case, then it is known that the meaning of His statement: And the intoxication of death will come in truth is: And the intoxication of death will come to you, O man, in truth. “That is what you were avoiding.” If that is the case, then the correctness of what we have said is clear.
50:22: And His statement, Indeed, you were heedless of this, God Almighty says: It will be said to him: You were heedless of what you witnessed today, O human, of the horrors and hardships. So We removed your veil, meaning: We made that clear to you and showed it to your eyes, until you saw it and witnessed it, and the heedlessness was removed from you. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this, although they differed about the one to whom this was said. Some of them said: The one to whom this was said is the unbeliever. Others said: He is the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: It is all creation, from jinn to humans. Mention of those who said: He is an infidel. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, you were in heedlessness of this, so We removed your veil from you, and that is the disbeliever. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then We removed your covering from you, he said: for the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: So We removed your cover from you. He said: Regarding the unbeliever. Mention of those who said: He is the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Indeed, you were heedless of this, he said: This is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Indeed, you were heedless of this matter, O Muhammad. You were with the people in their ignorance. So We have removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp. According to this interpretation of what Ibn Zayd said, this speech must be an address from God to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was in ignorance during the pre-Islamic period of what He had sent him with, so He revealed to him the gift that he had received during the pre-Islamic period, so his sight penetrated with faith and became clear to him until it was established in him and he became sharp-sighted because of it. It was mentioned that he said: It is all of creation, from the wolves and the human beings. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Yaqub ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri told me: I asked al-Husayn ibn Abd God ibn Ubayd God ibn Abbas about that, and he said: He means the righteous and the wicked, So We have removed your covering from you, and your sight today is sharp. He said: And the covering was removed from the righteous and the wicked, and they saw everything that they would become. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of His statement, So We removed your covering from you, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, Then We removed your covering from you, he said: Life after death. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Indeed, you were in heedlessness of this, so We removed your veil from you, he said: He witnessed the Hereafter. His saying, So your sight today is sharp, means: You are a sharp-sighted person, aware of what you were unaware of in this world. It is from their saying: So-and-so is perceptive about this matter, meaning he has knowledge of it, and he has insight into this matter, meaning knowledge. It was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak that he said: The meaning of So your sight today is sharp is the tongue of the scales. I think that he meant by that that his knowledge and awareness of what he did in the past in this world is a just witness against him, so he likened his sight to the tongue of the scales by which the truth is weighed and the amount due to its people is known, whether it is more or less. Likewise, the knowledge of the one who comes to the Resurrection of what he acquired in this world is a witness against him like the tongue of the scales.
50:23: God Almighty says: And the companion of this man who will bring him on the Day of Resurrection will say, He will be with him as a driver and a witness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And his companion said, ‘This is what I have ready.’ Al-Mulk. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And his companion said, ‘This is what I have ready’… to the end of the verse, he said: This is his driver who was assigned to him, and he recited, And every soul will come with a driver and a witness. And His statement, This is what is with Me ready, is what the Almighty says, informing us about what this person’s companion will say when he meets his Lord, Lord, this is what is with Me ready, meaning: This that is with Me is prepared and preserved. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, This is what I have ready, he said: The ready is what he took, and the driver and the guard brought it with him together.
50:24: And his saying, Throw into Hell every obstinate disbeliever there is something omitted in it that is dispensed with by the apparent meaning of it, which is: It is said, Throw into Hell, or God Almighty said, Throw, so He directed the command to the companion, and it is in one word, in the manner of addressing two people. There are two aspects of interpretation for that: The first: That the companion has the meaning of two, like the messenger, and the noun that has the singular form in the singular, dual, and plural, so He returned his saying, Throw into Hell to the meaning. The second: That it is as some of the Arabs used to say, which is that the Arabs command one person and a group with what they command two people, so they say to the man, Woe to you, saddle it and drive it away. He mentioned that he heard it from the Arabs, and he said: And one of them recited to me: I said to my friend, Don’t detain us by uprooting its roots and cutting down its wormwood. He said: Abu Tharwan recited to me: If you forbid me, O son of Affan, I will forbid, and if you call me, I will be an impregnable presence. He said: It is narrated that this is because a man has at least two helpers in his camels and sheep, and likewise the minimum number of companions is three. So the speech of one of them was directed towards his two companions, and he said: Don’t you see that poets are the most frequently spoken thing, my friend, my intimate friend? Imru' al-Qais said: My friend, I passed by Umm Jundub, and he broke the hearts of the tormented ones. Then he said: Didn't you see that whenever I came to a new place, I found it fragrant, even if it was not fragrant? So he returned to the one, and the first speech was two. He said: And some of them recited to me: My two friends, come to me while I am idle. See if you see any light from Dhu Abanin or from lightning. Some of them say: We see light. Every stubborn disbeliever means: every stubborn denier of the oneness of God, and he is stubborn about the truth and the path of guidance.
50:25: And his saying, Preventing goodness, Qatada used to say about goodness in this context: It is the obligatory zakat. Bishr told us that: Yazid told us that: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that it is every right due to God, or to a human being in his money, and the good in this situation is money. We said that this is the correct statement, because God Almighty mentioned it in His statement preventing good that it prevents good and did not specify one thing over another, so this applies to every good that can be prevented by someone seeking it. His saying aggressive means: someone who is aggressive towards people with his tongue, with obscenities and vulgarity in speech, and with his hand, with force and oppression unjustly. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, that he was strict in his speech, his conduct, and his command. His saying doubtful means: doubting the oneness of God and His ability to do whatever He wills. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying doubtful means doubtful.
50:26: God Almighty says: He who associates others with God and worships with Him another deity from among His creation, throw him into the severe punishment. He says: Throw him into the severe punishment of Hell.
50:27: God Almighty says: The companion of man, the disbeliever who prevents good, said: He is his devil who was assigned to him in this world. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, His companion said, ‘Our Lord, I did not make him transgress.’ He said: His companion was his devil. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, His companion said, he said: Satan was assigned to him. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Who has set up with God another god, he is the polytheist. His companion said, ‘Our Lord, I did not make him transgress.’ He said: His companion is Satan. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: His companion said, ‘Our Lord, I did not make him transgress.’ He said: His companion was Satan. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, His companion said, ‘Our Lord, I did not make him transgress.’ He said: His companion is his Satan. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, His companion said, ‘Our Lord, I did not make him transgress,’ His companion from among the jinn said, Our Lord, I did not make him transgress. He disavowed him. And His statement, Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, means: I did not make him a transgressor, transgressing to what he did not have. Rather, what he means by that is disbelief in God. But he was far astray, meaning: but he was on a path that deviated far from the path of guidance. God Almighty informed us about the words of the disbeliever’s companion on the Day of Resurrection, as a way to inform His servants that they will disown one another on the Day of Resurrection. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about his statement, Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, he said: He disavowed him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad told me: Abdullah bin Abi Bakr told us: Jaafar told us: I heard Abu Imran say about His statement, Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, that he disavowed it.
50:28: And His statement, Do not dispute before Me, God Almighty says: God said to these polytheists, whose description He described, and the description of their companions from the devils, Do not dispute before Me today, and I have presented to you in this world before your dispute with the threat for whoever disbelieves in Me, disobeys Me, and opposes My command and prohibition in My books and on the tongues of My messengers. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad told me: Abdullah bin Abi Bakr told us: Jaafar told us: I heard Abu Imran say about the statement of God, And I have already brought you the threat, he said: With the Qur’an. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Do not dispute before Me, he said: They made excuses without an excuse, so God invalidated their argument and rejected their statement. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Do not dispute before me while I have already brought you the threat, he said: He says: I have commanded you and forbidden you. He said: This is the son of Adam and his companion from the jinn. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Abu Ja`far on the authority of Al-Rabi` who said: I said to Abu Al-`Aliyah, Do not dispute in my presence, for I have already brought you the threat. Abu Ja`far Al-Tabari said: I think he said: They are the people of polytheism. And he said in another verse, Then on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord, so they are the people of the Qiblah.
50:29: God Almighty says, informing us of what He will say to the polytheists and their jinn companions on the Day of Resurrection, when they will disavow each other: What will change the statement that I made to you in this world, which is His statement I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together, nor the judgment that I decreed for them therein? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The word is not changed with Me, I have decided what I am going to decide. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The word cannot be changed with Me, he said: I have decided what I am going to decide. And His saying, And I am not unjust to the servants, means: I will not punish any of My creation for the crime of another, nor will I hold any of them responsible for a sin other than his own, and thus torment him for it.
50:30: And His statement, On the Day We will say to Hell, meaning: I will not be unjust to the servants on the Day We will say to Hell, Are you filled? That is on the Day of Resurrection. And the Day We will say is from the word of injustice. And the Most High said to Hell on the Day of Resurrection, Are you filled? because of His previous promise to it that He would fill it with jinn and people all together. As for his statement, Is there any more? the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: Its meaning is: There is no more. They said: Rather, God says to it: Are you full after He places His foot in it, so some of it withdraws into some of it and says: Enough, enough, out of its constriction. Then when He says to it when it has become like this: Are you full? It then says: Is there any more? Meaning: There is no more, because of its intense fullness and the constriction of some of it into some of it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, On the Day We will say to Hell, ‘Are you filled?’ and it will say, ‘Are there any more?’ Ibn Abbas said: God, the King, Blessed and Exalted be He, had previously said, I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together. So when the people were resurrected and brought forth, and the enemies of God were driven to the Fire in groups, they began to rush into Hell, group by group. Nothing was thrown into Hell but that it went into it, and nothing would fill it. It said, Did you not swear that you would fill me with jinn and people all together? Then he put his foot in it, and I said when he put his foot in it, It is done, for I am already filled, so I have no more. And nothing would fill it, until it felt the touch of what was placed on it, and it felt constricted when what was placed on it was placed, so it was filled with the space of a needle. Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And she says, ‘Is there more?’ He said: God promised him that He would fill it, so he said, Why don’t I fulfill it for you? She said, Is there a way out? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, The Day We will say to Hell, ‘Are you filled?’ and it will say, ‘Are there any more?’ Ibn Ibn Abbas used to say: God, the Sovereign, had previously uttered a word from Him, I will surely fill Hell. Nothing will be thrown into it but will go into it, nothing will fill it, until not one of its people remains who will not have entered it, and nothing will fill it. Then the Lord will come to it and place His foot upon it, then say to it, ‘Are you filled, O Hell?’ It will say, ‘Enough, enough. I am filled. You have filled me with jinn and mankind, so there is no more.’ Ibn Abbas said: Nothing would fill it until it felt the touch of the foot of God, the Most High, and it became constricted, and there was not in it the space of a needle. Others said: Rather, the meaning of increase me is is there more?, meaning to increase. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein bin Thabit told us on the authority of Anas, who said: He will be thrown into Hell and it will say: Is there more? three times, until he places his foot in it, and it will move away from one another, and it will say: Enough, enough, three times. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, On the Day We will say to Hell, ‘Are you filled?’ and it will say, ‘Are there any more?’ because it has been filled, and Are there any more? means, Is anyone left? He said: These are the two interpretations of this, and God knows best. He said: They said this and this. The first of the two opinions on this matter, in my opinion, is the correct one, which says: It means asking for more, is there anything I can add? We said that this is the more correct of the two sayings due to the authenticity of the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which says: Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam al-Ajli told me: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Tafawi told us: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will not wrong any of His creation in the least, and he will be thrown into the Fire, which will say, ‘Is there more?’ until he places his foot on it. Then it will be filled, and some parts will be brought together, and it will say, ‘Enough, enough.’” Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam told us: Al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Anas who said: “Hell will continue to say: ‘Is there more?’ until God places His foot on it, and it will say: ‘Indeed, indeed.’ And there will continue to be surplus in Paradise until God creates a creation and inhabits it with the surplus of Paradise.” Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me: Ibn ‘Alayh narrated to us: Ayoub and Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: Paradise and Hell argued. Paradise said: Why is it that only the poor and the downtrodden among people enter me? Hell said: Why is it that only the tyrants and the arrogant enter me? He said: You are My mercy; I strike with you whomever I will, and you are My punishment; I strike with you whomever I will, and each of you will have its fill. As for Paradise, God creates for it from His creation whomever He wills. As for Hell, they will be thrown into it and it will say: Are there any more? And they will be thrown into it and it will say: Are there any more? Until He sets His foot in it. Then it will be filled, and some parts will close in on each other and it will say: Enough, enough. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Thawr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Paradise and Hell argued. Paradise said: Why do only the poor enter me? Hell said: Why do only the tyrants and the arrogant enter me? Hell said to Hell: You are My punishment; I afflict with you whomever I will. And it said to Paradise: You are My mercy; I afflict with you whomever I will, and each of you will have its fill. As for Paradise, God creates for it what He wills, but as for Hell, they will be thrown into it and it will say: Are there any more? Until He places His foot in it. Then it will be filled and some parts will withdraw into others, saying: Enough, enough." Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Hell will continue to throw people into it and will say: ‘Is there more?’ until the Lord of the Worlds sets foot, and some parts of it will withdraw into others and say: ‘Enough, enough, by Your glory and Your generosity!’ And there will continue to be surplus in Paradise until God creates for it a creation and inhabits them in the surplus of Paradise.” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad told us: Aban Al-Attar told us: Qatada told us on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Hell will continue to say, ‘Is there more?’ until the Lord of the Worlds places His foot in it. Then some parts will withdraw into others and say, ‘By Your glory, enough, enough.’ And there will continue to be surplus in Paradise until God creates a creation and places it in the surplus of Paradise.” He said: Amr bin Asim Al-Kalabi told us, he said: Al-Mu’tamir told us on the authority of his father, he said: Qatada told us on the authority of Anas, he said: Hell will not cease to say: Is there more? And he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Or something like that. Ziyad ibn Ayoub narrated: Abdul Wahhab ibn Ata’ al-Khaffaf narrated from Saeed from Qatadah from Anas from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who said: “Paradise and Hell argued. Hell said: ‘The tyrants and the arrogant will enter me.’ Paradise said: ‘The poor and needy will enter me.’ So God, the Exalted, revealed to Paradise: ‘You are My mercy; I will strike with you whomever I will.’ And He revealed to Hell: ‘You are My punishment; I will strike with you whomever I will. Each of you will have its own fill. As for Hell, it will say: ‘Are there any more?’ until he sets his foot in it. Then it will say: ‘Enough, enough.’” The Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) statement: “Hell will not cease saying: ‘Are there any more?’” clearly indicates that this means seeking more, not denying something, because His statement ‘will not cease’ is evidence of the continuity of one statement after another.
50:31: God Almighty means by His saying, And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far away, that Paradise will be brought near and brought close to those who feared their Lord, so they feared His punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, meaning: And it will be brought near, not far.
50:32: And His saying, This is what you are promised, means: He said to them: This is what you are promised, O righteous ones, that you will enter it and dwell in it. His saying, For every penitent means: for every person who returns from disobeying God to obeying Him, repenting from his sins. The commentators differed on the meaning of this. Some of them said: It is the one who glorifies God, and some of them said: It is the one who repents. We have mentioned their differences on this in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. However, we will mention in this place what we did not mention there. Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: For every one who turns back means for every one who glorifies God. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muslim al-Awar, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Al-Awab is the one who glorifies God. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Yahya bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Ghania told me: My father told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, regarding the statement of God, For every one who turns back [to Him] and is mindful, he said: He is the one who remembers God in the privacy. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus bin Khabab, on the authority of Mujahid: For every one who turns back [to God] is a guardian. He said: The one who remembers his sins and seeks forgiveness for them. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, This is what you are promised to everyone who frequently turns back. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Khajah, on the authority of Isa al-Hannat, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: He is the one who remembers his sins in private and seeks forgiveness for them. Hafiz means obedient to God and prays often. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, For every one who turns back [to God] is a guardian, he said: The one who turns back [to God] is the one who turns back to God’s obedience and returns to it. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Yunus bin Khabab, regarding His statement, For every one who turns back [to God], He is Preserver of [His] mercy. He said: The man remembers his sins and asks God for forgiveness for them. And his saying, Preserver, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: He preserved his sins until he repented from them. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the repentant and the preserver. He said: He preserves his sins until he turns away from them. Others said: It means that he is a guardian of God’s obligations and what He has entrusted him with. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Hafiz means: Hafiz is the guardian of what God has entrusted to him of His right and His blessings. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty described this repentant, returning person as a Guardian, and He did not specify that he guards one type of obedience over another. Rather, it should be general, as He, the Most High, is general. It should be said: He is a Guardian of everything that he brought to his Lord of the obligatory acts of obedience and the sins that he committed in the past, for which he repented and sought forgiveness.
50:33: And his saying: Whoever fears the Most Merciful in secret means: Whoever fears God in this world before meeting Him, obeys Him, and follows His command. As for min in his statement: Whoever fears, there are two ways of parsing: the accusative case is to follow kull in his statement: for every one who turns back, and the nominative case is to resume, and what is meant by it is the reward of whoever fears the Most Gracious in secret. It will be said to him: Enter Paradise. So then his statement: “Enter it in peace” is an answer to the reward, before which the statement was implied, and it was made an action for all, because min can be in the doctrine of all. His saying, And he came with a heart repentant, means: And he came to God with a heart repentant of his sins, turning from what God hates to what pleases Him. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And he came with a heart turning in repentance: meaning turning to his Lord and turning towards Him.
