Others said: It is the night prayer at any time. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me: Ubaid God bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid: And during a part of the night glorify Him. He said: During the entire night. Mujahid's statement on this matter is closer to being correct, because God, the Exalted, said: And during part of the night glorify Him. He did not specify a specific time during the night. If that is the case, then it applies to all hours of the night. If the matter is as we have described, then it is more like a command to pray the Maghrib and Isha prayers than a command to pray the Isha prayer, because they are both performed at night. His saying: And at the end of prostration means: Glorify your Lord with praise at the end of prostration in your prayer. The interpreters differed about the meaning of the glorification that God commanded His Prophet to glorify Him after prostration. Some of them said: It refers to prayer. They said: They are the two rak’ahs that are prayed after the Maghrib prayer. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, who said: I asked Ali about the ends of prostration, and he said: The two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ali told us: Ibn Jurayj told us on the authority of Mujahid: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: And the ends of al-Sajdah 32:the two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer. Abu Kurayb told us: Mus`ab bin Salam told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, who said: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: The ends of prostration are the two rak`ahs after the Maghrib prayer. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement: and the ends of prostration, he said: The two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer. He said: Yahya told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Asim bin Damrah, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ali, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The ends of prostration are the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer. Ali bin Hilal told me: Muammil told us: Hammad told us: Ali bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Aws bin Khalid, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer are the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Alwan ibn Abi Malik, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: The ends of prostration are the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid: The two rak’ahs after al-Sajdah 32:the number of rak’ahs of the Maghrib prayer. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding this verse: And during part of the night glorify Him and at the end of prostration and at the setting of the stars, he said: The two rak`ahs before dawn and the two rak`ahs after sunset. Shu`bah said: I do not know which of them is prostration, and I do not know which of them is at the setting of the stars. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: and the ends of prostration, he said: Mujahid used to say: Two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer. Muhammad bin Saeed told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And the ends of prostration, he said: They are the two prostrations after the Maghrib prayer. Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Fadil told us, on the authority of Rashdin bin Kurayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: O Ibn Abbas, two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer, after prostration. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul-Hakam told me: Abu Zur’ah and Hibat God Rashid told us: Haywah bin Shureih told us: Abu Sakhr told us that he heard Abu Mu’awiyah Al-Bajali from the people of Kufa say: I heard Abu Al-Sahbaa Al-Bakri say: I asked Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, about the ends of prostration. He said: They are two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer. Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me: Baqiyah told us: Jarir told us: Himyar bin Yazid Al-Rahbi told us on the authority of Krayb bin Yazid Al-Rahbi: Jubayr bin Nufayr used to walk to him. He said: If he prayed the two rak’ahs before dawn and the two rak’ahs after sunset, he would make them shorter. He explained the setting of the stars and the ending of prostration. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Isa bin Yazid, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And the ends of al-Sajdah 32:the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: It was said: The ends of prostration are the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer. He said: Anbasa told us on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir on the authority of Mujahid: And the ends of al-Sajdah 32:the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer. He said: Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Ata’ who said: Ali said: The two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer. Ibn Al-Barqi told us: Amr bin Abi Salamah told us: Al-Awza’i was asked about the two rak’ahs after Maghrib. He said: They are in the Book of God: So glorify Him and after prostration. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement: And the ends of prostration, he said: The two rak’ahs after the sunset prayer. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the ends of prostration he said: Two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer. Others said: What he meant by his saying: and after prostration is the glorification of God after the obligatory prayers, not the prayer after them. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ibn Abi Nujayh told us on the authority of Mujahid: Ibn Abbas said about So glorify Him and after al-Sajdah 32:It is the glorification after the prayer. Muhammad ibn Amur told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, and at the ends of prostration, he said: Ibn Abbas used to say: glorification. Ibn Amr said in his hadith: in all prayers. Al-Harith said in his hadith: at the end of all prayers. Others said: They are the voluntary prayers after the obligatory prayers. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yunus bin Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: and the ends of al-Sajdah 32:the voluntary prayers. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: The two rak’ahs after Maghrib, because of the consensus of the people of interpretation on this. And were it not for what you mentioned of their consensus on it, you would have seen that the saying on this matter is what Ibn Zayd said, because God, may He be glorified and exalted, did not specify one prayer with that over another, rather He included the ends of all prayers, so He said: and the ends of prostration, and there is no proof that it is meant by it the ends of one prayer over another, and there is no proof of acceptance of it from a report or reason. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement: and the ends of prostration. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Kufa, except for Asim and Al-Kisa’i, recited and the ends of prostration with a kasra on the alif, as it is the source of adbara idbara. Asim, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Amr recited and the ends with a fatha on the alif, as the plural of dabar and adbar. The correct pronunciation, in my opinion, is the opening of the word dabar.
50:41: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And listen, O Muhammad, to the shout on the Day of Resurrection, the day when a caller will call out from a nearby place. He said that he calls for it from the rock of Jerusalem. Who said that? Ali bin Sahl told me: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Bishr, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ka’b, who said: And listen on the Day when the crier will call from a place nearby. An angel standing on the rock of Jerusalem will call: O decayed bones and disjointed limbs, God commands you to gather for the passing of judgment. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And listen on the Day when the crier will call from a place nearby. He said: We were told that he would call from the Holy House from the rock, which is the middle of the earth. Kaab told us: It is the closest land to the sky by eighteen miles. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: On the Day when the crier will call from a nearby place. He said: I have been informed that he will call from the rock in Jerusalem. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And listen on the Day when the crier will call from a place nearby. He said: It is the shout. Ali bin Sahl told me: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: Some of our companions told me, on the authority of Al-Agharr, on the authority of Muslim bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ibn Buraydah, on the authority of his father Buraydah, who said: An angel is standing on the rock of Jerusalem, putting his fingers in his ears, calling out. I said: What is he calling out? He said: He says: O people, come to the accounting. He said: So they come as God said: As if they were locusts scattered (al-Qamar 54:7).
50:42: And His statement: On the Day they hear the Shout in truth, God Almighty says: On the Day when creation hears the Shout of Resurrection from the graves in truth, meaning there is no command to respond to God until the place of reckoning. And His saying, That is the Day of Resurrection, means that God Almighty says: The Day when the people of the graves will emerge from their graves.
50:43: God Almighty says: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and cause the living to die, and to Us is the destination of all of them on the Day of Resurrection. The Day the earth will split open and reveal them in haste. God Almighty says: And to Us is their destination on the Day the earth will split open. So today is related to destiny.
50:44: And his statement: The earth will split open over them means: The earth will split open over them. And his statement: Quickly and Quickly is in the accusative case as a state of the ha' and the mim in his statement about them. The meaning is: On the day the earth will split open over them and they will be destroyed from it quickly. So the indication of his statement: On the day the earth will split open over them was sufficient for mentioning that. His saying: That is an easy gathering for Us, means: Their gathering is an easy gathering for Us at the time of reckoning.
50:45: God Almighty says: We, O Muhammad, know best what these polytheists say about their slander against God, their denial of His signs, and their denial of God’s ability to resurrect after death. And you are not a tyrant over them. He says: You are not a power over them. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And you are not a tyrant over them. He said: Do not be tyrannical toward them. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And you are not a tyrant over them, for God Almighty disliked determinism, forbade it, and presented it in it. Al-Farra’ said: He placed the tyrant in the place of the ruler in determinism, and he said: Al-Mufaddal recited to me: And on the day of sorrow, when Ma'ad was gathered, and the people were all in debt except us. We disobeyed his mighty will until we became the hollow of a thousand teachers It is narrated: Al-Jawf. He said: By Al-Jabbar he meant: Al-Mundhir of his authority. He said: It was said that the meaning of his statement, And you are not a compeller over them is that you were not sent to force them to Islam, rather you were sent as a reminder, so he reminded. He said: The Arabs do not say fa’al from af’alta. They do not say: this is kharaj, meaning exit, nor do they say dakhal, meaning entrance. Rather they say fa’al, from fa’ala, and they say kharaj from kharaja, and dakhal from dakhalat, and qital from qatal. He said: The Arabs say with one letter: daraka, from adarak, and it is anomalous. He said: If you say that the tyrant has this meaning, then it is correct. He said: I heard some Arabs say: He forced him to do something, meaning: He compelled him. So the tyrant in this language is correct, meaning: He subdues them and compels them. And His statement, So remind with the Qur’an whoever fears My threat, God Almighty says: So remind, O Muhammad, with this Qur’an that I revealed to him whoever fears the threat that I have threatened whoever disobeys Me and opposes My command. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me: Hakam Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Amr Al-Mala’i, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They said, O Messenger of God, if you had frightened us! So the verse was revealed: And remind by the Qur’an whoever fears My threat. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Sayyar Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, who said: They said: O Messenger of God, if you would remind us! So he mentioned something similar.
